sections.h2: Which Sullivan County offices deal with property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, and neither sets the rate. The Property Assessor, Donna Whitaker, values every parcel from 3411 Highway 126, Suite 103, in Blountville (423-323-6455, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). The Trustee collects the money at 1651 Blountville Boulevard, Suite 104, Blountville, TN 37617 (423-323-6464, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.). The County Commission picks the rate each year.

The Trustee also keeps two seasonal counters, in Bristol at 801 Anderson Street, Room 139 (Thursday and Friday) and in Kingsport at 225 West Center Street, #101 (Monday through Wednesday). Both run only from October 1 to March 15, close from 1:30 to 2:30 p.m. for lunch and shut on holidays and election days.

A house inside Bristol, Kingsport or Bluff City can draw a city bill as well as the county one, according to the Trustee's FAQ. Ask the city about its own rate and due date.

sections.h2: What is Sullivan County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Sullivan County fills the northeast corner of Tennessee along the Virginia line. It was cut from Washington County in 1779 and covers 430 square miles, of which 413 are land. Kingsport is the largest city, and Bristol, Bluff City and a slice of Johnson City also fall inside. Blountville, the county seat, is the only unincorporated county seat in Tennessee.

The land runs from Ridge-and-Valley ridges in the west to the Blue Ridge in the east, where Holston Mountain tops out at 4,284 feet. Kingsport is where the North and South Forks of the Holston River meet. Three school systems serve the county: Bristol Tennessee City Schools, Kingsport City School District and Sullivan County Schools, so a buyer's zone depends on the address.

Census Bureau QuickFacts show a lower price level than nearby Sumner County:

  • 163,759 residents in July 2025, up 3.5% from April 2020
  • 77,633 housing units, 72.1% occupied by their owners
  • Median owner-occupied value of $213,300 (2020 to 2024)
  • Median gross rent of $889 and median household income of $58,807
  • 771 building permits in 2025

sections.h2: How is a Sullivan County property tax bill figured?
sections.html:
The Trustee's FAQ gives the formula: 25 percent of the property's value, times the county rate per $100. The 2025 county rate listed there is $1.6129 per $100 of assessed value. On a $250,000 house, the assessed value is $62,500, which at that rate comes to about $1,008 for the year.

The bill covers January 1 through December 31 of the tax year. Business furniture and equipment are taxed too, and owners must file a personal property schedule each year. The Assessor adds that the next county-wide reappraisal is set for 2027, so values can change again before long.

sections.h2: When is Sullivan County property tax due, and how can I pay?
sections.html:
Tax comes due on the first Monday in October and can be paid without penalty through the last day of February. Today is November 15, 2026, so the 2026 bill is open and nothing is late. The Trustee lists no early-payment discount. On March 1 the balance turns delinquent and 1.5 percent interest is added each month.

Ways to pay include:

  • In person in Blountville, Bristol or Kingsport
  • By mail to PO Box 550, Blountville, TN 37617, or the Blountville drop box
  • Online or by phone, with a 2.5 percent card fee or $1.25 e-check fee that goes to the processor
  • At Bank of Tennessee branches with the notice, cash or check only

Installments are allowed between October 1 and February 28, though the owner must track the balance. No notice is required by law, so a missing bill does not excuse interest.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Sullivan County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's office, then the county board of equalization, which the state schedule places on June 1. An appeal to the State Board of Equalization is due by August 1 or within 45 days of the county board's notice, whichever is later. For tax year 2026 the August date has passed, so an owner holding a later notice should call 615-401-7883 to check the 45-day window.

The state's guidance says the best proof for a house is sales of comparable homes, with differences in size, age, condition and location explained. An appraisal may also be offered. A statement that a house is overvalued, with no figure behind it, is usually not enough. The taxpayer must still pay the undisputed part of the bill on time, along with any older delinquent tax.

sections.h2: What tax relief is there for Sullivan County homeowners?
sections.html:
The state relief rebate covers owners who live in their home and are 65 or older, disabled, or a qualifying disabled veteran or widow of one. The income cap for the elderly and disabled is $38,470 combined, spouse included. Bring proof of income, a Social Security card and proof of residency and age. Call 423-323-6470 or 423-323-6469 for an appointment.

The signed voucher must come back to a Trustee office each year by April 5, and bank branches do not accept it. Sullivan County does not offer a tax freeze program.

sections.h2: Can a Sullivan County owner qualify for greenbelt or an exemption?
sections.html:
The Assessor's office also manages Greenbelt and Forestry assessments, which value qualifying farm and timber land by use instead of market price. The state calendar sets March 15 as the greenbelt application deadline and May 20 for exemption applications. Owners of acreage should ask the Assessor about both before listing, because a buyer may inherit the tax treatment only if the land still qualifies after the sale.

Anyone who owns a business furnishing or equipment on January 1 may owe personal property tax even after closing the shop. The Trustee says the business must be formally closed with the right agencies.

sections.h2: Who pays the tax when a Sullivan County house sells?
sections.html:
The owner of record on January 1 receives the notice, even if the house sells later in the year. The Trustee says new owners still must see that the tax is paid on time, and to follow the settlement statement for the split. Where a lender escrows taxes, the bill goes to the mortgage company.

A seller with unpaid tax should settle the balance with the Trustee before closing. Interest can be removed only by a court order or an assessment change from the State Board or the Assessor, so a late bill rarely gets waived.

faqs.q: What is the Sullivan County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Trustee lists the 2025 county rate at $1.6129 per $100 of assessed value. Homes are assessed at 25 percent of value, and cities may add their own tax.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Sullivan County taxes early?
faqs.a: No discount is listed. Taxes can be paid without penalty from October 1 through February 28, and the Trustee permits installments in that window.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Sullivan County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Pay at the Trustee in Blountville, or at the seasonal Bristol and Kingsport counters from October 1 through March 15. Bank of Tennessee branches also take cash or check payments with the notice.

faqs.q: Does Sullivan County offer a property tax freeze?
faqs.a: No. The Trustee says Sullivan County does not currently offer a freeze program, though the state tax relief rebate is available to qualifying seniors, disabled owners and veterans.

faqs.q: When is the next Sullivan County reappraisal?
faqs.a: The Assessor's page lists 2027 as the next county-wide reappraisal. The Assessor's 2025 update described a reappraisal that year, with revaluation notices going out in the spring.
